title: 墨西哥活牛：重启在即，一个口岸真能救急？
speaker: Alina Peng

segments.en: it did finally make its way to the US earlier this year in June and so I think the risk calculus was we have been able to manage the spread there are very few active cases currently in Texas now
segments.zh: 今年6月，螺旋蛆虫终于传入美国。我认为风险评估是，我们已经能够控制传播，目前得克萨斯州活跃病例很少。

segments.en: so those imports from Mexico are expected to start in the end of this month with one port in Arizona it's not the biggest port so hopefully that reopening goes well such that the USDA will open other ports and we'll see more significant flows
segments.zh: 因此，墨西哥进口预计本月底重启，首先在亚利桑那州的一个口岸，虽然不是最大的口岸，但希望重启顺利，以便美国农业部开放更多口岸，带来更显著的流量。

segments.en: but that one port alone I don't think necessarily will make a large national difference though definitely I think regional meat packing plants should hopefully start to see some reprieve soon
segments.zh: 但仅这一个口岸，我认为不一定能带来全国性的大变化。不过，区域性肉类加工厂应该很快会看到一些缓解。

segments.en: Alina before we wrap up here you know they're shutting down plants is it though with the anticipation that eventually they'll reopen them or I am curious that when to shut them down do they stay down and what that means for overall future meat supply here the US
segments.zh: Alina，在结束前，我想问，他们关闭工厂是预期最终会重新开放吗？还是说关闭了就永久关闭？这对美国未来整体肉类供应意味着什么？
